title: Fabricate a flexible hose
subject: General
assumptions: The hose lay line runs straight along the taped section, showing the hose was not twisted while marking.
The wheel is free of cracks, chips or gouges and the guard is in place over it.
Air supply is coupled to the tool inlet and regulated to the tool's rated inlet pressure.
The cover is removed cleanly around the full circumference at the fitting location, leaving continuous bare wire braid with no cover tags or rubber remnants.
The exposed wire braid shows no cut, nicked, broken or splayed strands and the inner tube is not exposed or scored.
The stripped length equals the fitting socket insertion depth, so the cover ends where the socket will seat.
openQuestions: Every check, error mode and evidence item in this pack was drafted by packs/compile_pack.py from the procedure sheet and handbook, and has not been reviewed by a subject-matter expert.

The AIM procedure sheet documents no steps for 'Assemble the End Fitting', 'Proof-Test the Hose Assembly', yet the task title and the sheet's own equipment list call for that work. Those steps were drafted from the handbook and the reference video and carry `origin: drafted`. Confirm with AIM whether they form part of the graded submission, and ask for a corrected procedure sheet if they do.

The campus step list ends at 'Verify the cuts', yet the task title says fabricate and the equipment list names MS fittings, mandrel and hydraulic fluid. Does the graded deliverable include end-fitting assembly and proof test, or only a cut blank?
The handbook's 5–8 percent is stated as installation slack (p. 9-21); the campus sheet applies it to cut length. An SME must confirm the allowance is intended to be added to the fabricated length.
Which hose specification and pressure class students use, since the cover-slitting step applies to high-pressure hose only and the lubricant caution depends on synthetic-fluid compatibility.
What proof-test pressure and medium the campus will accept as 'the manufacturer's specification' in a shop setting, and whether a burst test stand is actually available to students.

steps.text: Measure the route that the hose needs to take.

checks.text: The recorded final hose dimension equals the measured route length plus 5–8 percent of that length.
checks.src: Sheet: add 5-8% of total length. Handbook p.9-21: "provide slack or bend in the hose line from 5 to 8 percent of its total length".

checks.text: The tape is run along the actual routing path through every bend, not pulled straight between end points.
checks.src: Sheet note 1: "Use a tape measure to map the distance"; a straight-line reading understates the route.

checks.text: Measured route length, the slack allowance and the resulting final dimension are written down before marking.
checks.src: Sheet equipment list includes pen & paper; worked example shows 24" + 1.9" = 25.9" recorded.

checks.text: The planned route contains no bend tighter than the minimum bend radius listed for that hose size.
checks.src: "Never use less than the recommended minimum bend radius specified for the hose"; radii tabulated in Figure 9-37.

errors.text: Slack allowance omitted, so the hose is cut to the bare measured route length and loads the fittings when pressurized.
Route measured as a straight line between end points, ignoring bends, giving a short final dimension.
Arithmetic or unit error in adding the 5–8 percent allowance, or the figure never recorded before marking.

steps.text: Choose a hose and fitting assembly.

checks.text: The dash number printed on the hose lay line and the dash numbers on the nipple, B-nut and collar are identical.
checks.src: Procedure sheet requires corresponding dash numbers; handbook p.9-19: "When the dash number of the hose corresponds with the dash number of the tubing, the proper size hose is being used."

checks.text: The hose lay line markings are legible and show specification number, size, and quarter/year of manufacture.
checks.src: "Most hydraulic hose is marked to identify its type, the quarter and year of manufacture"; markings "repeated at intervals of not more than 9 inches."

checks.text: The selected hose type and pressure class are approved for the system's fluid and operating pressure per the applicable manual.
checks.src: "to make the correct hose selection, always refer to the applicable aircraft maintenance or parts manual"; Skydrol hose marked "Skydrol use."

checks.text: The MS-type nipple, socket/collar and B-nut show no thread damage, nicks or distortion that would bar reuse.
checks.src: "detachable fittings used on flexible hoses may be detached and reused if they are not damaged; otherwise, new fittings must be used."

errors.text: Hose and fitting dash numbers do not match, so the fitting ID differs from the hose ID.
Hose material is incompatible with the system fluid (e.g., Buna-N or neoprene selected for Skydrol).
Fitting assembly is mixed from different kits or a damaged/deformed reusable fitting is selected.

checks.text: The tape band's marked edge sits at the finished length: measured route plus 5–8 percent added allowance.
checks.src: Procedure sheet: add 5-8% to measured distance. Handbook p.9-19/9-21: "provide slack or bend in the hose line from 5 to 8 percent of its total length".

checks.text: Masking tape is wrapped evenly and square to the hose axis, its edge forming one continuous unspiraled line around the circumference.
checks.src: Sheet requires tape "wrapped evenly around the hose"; the tape edge is the cut guide, so it must be a single crisp perpendicular line.

checks.text: The hose lay line runs straight along the taped section, showing the hose was not twisted while marking.
checks.src: Handbook: "This stripe should not spiral around the hose." Stated for installation; applying it to the marking step needs SME confirmation.

checks.text: The dash number and lay-line markings needed for identification remain legible and are not buried under the tape wrap.
checks.src: Sheet marks the hose on its lay line by dash number; markings must stay readable for fitting-size verification at assembly.

errors.text: Tape placed at the raw measured distance with the 5–8 percent expansion allowance omitted, so the hose is short but looks correctly marked.
Tape wrapped spirally or with a ragged, doubled edge, leaving no single defined cut line.
Tape applied loosely so it can slide along the hose, or wrapped over the dash number and lay line.

subtasks.label: Cut The Hose
subtasks.excluded: 3 [video], 3 [measurement] — held beside the frame, never folded into the criterion.

steps.text: Secure the hose into a table vise.

checks.text: The hose is clamped in the vise jaws, not hand-held or resting loose, before any cutting.
checks.src: Handbook p.9-19 Fig. 9-35 step 1: "Place hose in vise and cut to desired length using fine tooth hacksaw or cut off wheel."

checks.text: The taped cut line protrudes just past the jaw edge, clear of the jaws and unobstructed.
checks.src: Sheet note 1: "Protrude the taped location to the edge of the vise"; handbook is silent on mark placement.

checks.text: The hose runs horizontally through the jaws with its axis square to the jaw faces and no kink or bend in the clamped span.
checks.src: Sheet note 1: "Place the hose horizontally through the vise jaws."

checks.text: Jaws are closed only snug, so the hose is not stretched or compressed out of round.
checks.src: Sheet note 1: "snug against the hose without putting significant tension on it"; snugness judged only as jaws are closed.

errors.text: Vise over-tightened, flattening the hose and collapsing the synthetic inner tube while the outer cover still looks normal.
Taped mark clamped inside or behind the jaws, so the cut cannot be made at the mark or the blade will strike the vise.
Hose clamped too loosely or with excessive unsupported overhang, letting it rotate or whip and yielding an angled, ragged cut.

steps.text: Setup a pneumatic cut off wheel.

checks.text: A composite abrasive wheel — not a toothed or metal-cutting blade — is fitted to the tool.
checks.src: Sheet note 2: 'Connect a composite blade cut off wheel to a compressed air source.' Handbook only says 'cut off wheel' generically.

checks.text: The wheel is free of cracks, chips or gouges and the guard is in place over it.
checks.src: Implied by safe use of the sheet's specified cut off wheel; handbook gives no wheel-condition wording. Needs SME confirmation of guard requirement.

checks.text: Air supply is coupled to the tool inlet and regulated to the tool's rated inlet pressure.
checks.src: Sheet requires connection to 'a compressed air source'; the pressure figure comes from tool manufacturer data, not either source. Needs SME confirmation.

checks.text: Tool spins up true, with no wheel wobble or unusual vibration, before touching the hose.
checks.src: Sheet note 3 requires starting the wheel just before contact and a consistent whining noise, implying a verified free run-up.

errors.text: A cracked, expired or wrong-type wheel is mounted; it looks intact but can shatter at speed.
Regulator set above the tool's rated pressure, over-speeding the composite wheel.
Arbor nut left loose or wheel mounted without its flange/guard.
A toothed blade is fitted in place of the composite wheel, tearing the hose braid.

checks.text: The cut face is square to the hose axis, with no angled, stepped or ragged edge.
checks.src: Sheet: "Keep the blade as vertical as possible to create a clean cut"; handbook only says cut to length with hacksaw or cut off wheel.

checks.text: Cut end shows no splayed or unravelled wire braid and no melted, smeared or collapsed inner tube.

steps.text: Slit the hose cover down to the wire braid at the fitting location and twist the cover off with pliers.

checks.text: The cover is removed cleanly around the full circumference at the fitting location, leaving continuous bare wire braid with no cover tags or rubber remnants.
checks.src: Fig. 9-35 step 2: "slit cover with knife to wire braid... After slitting cover, twist off with pair of pliers." Step itself is supplemental, needs SME confirmation.

checks.text: The exposed wire braid shows no cut, nicked, broken or splayed strands and the inner tube is not exposed or scored.
checks.src: Fig. 9-35 step 2: "taking care to not damage underlying materials." Supplemental step; applicability requires SME confirmation.

checks.text: The stripped length equals the fitting socket insertion depth, so the cover ends where the socket will seat.
checks.src: Handbook only says "locate length of hose to be cut off"; no dimension given, so length comes from the fitting manufacturer. Needs SME confirmation.

checks.text: The hose is confirmed as high-pressure type before any cover is removed.
checks.src: Fig. 9-35: "NOTE: Step 2 applies to high-pressure hose only"; type established from lay-line spec number and parts manual.

errors.text: Knife cut passes through the wire braid into the synthetic inner tube, leaving a hose that looks assembled but will burst or leak.
Cover stripped from a medium- or low-pressure hose that does not require stripping, destroying its protective outer braid.
Cover stripped at the wrong location or to the wrong length, so the socket cannot seat on bare braid.
Ragged cover edge with torn tags or embedded cover fragments left on the braid.

steps.text: Place the hose in a vise and screw the socket onto the hose counterclockwise.

checks.text: The socket is run fully onto the hose so no bare wire braid or stripped cover shows between the socket lip and the hose cover.
checks.src: Handbook Fig. 9-35 step 3: "place hose in vise and screw socket on hose counterclockwise"; full-seating depth not stated verbatim — needs SME confirmation.

checks.text: The socket was threaded onto the hose by counterclockwise rotation, consistent with its left-hand thread.
checks.src: Handbook Fig. 9-35 step 3: "screw socket on hose counterclockwise"; direction is indistinguishable in a finished still. Supplemental step, needs SME confirmation.

checks.text: The hose cover and wire braid at the socket entry are undamaged, with no cut, unraveled or pushed-back strands.
checks.src: Handbook Fig. 9-35 cautions slitting cover "taking care to not damage underlying materials"; applied here provisionally, needs SME confirmation.

checks.text: The hose is held in the vise firmly without flattening, kinking or collapsing the inner tube.
checks.src: Handbook says only "place hose in vise"; clamping force qualitative and judged while clamped. Provisional, needs SME confirmation.

errors.text: Socket turned clockwise, gouging the cover and never engaging the left-hand thread while appearing installed.
Socket not run fully on, so the hose does not bottom and required nipple clearance cannot be achieved.
Vise jaws over-tightened, crushing or kinking the hose at the clamp point.

steps.text: Lubricate the inside of the hose and the nipple threads liberally.

checks.text: A wet lubricant film is visible on the hose inner tube bore and on the nipple threads before assembly.
checks.src: Fig. 9-35 step 4: "Lubricate inside of hose and nipple threads liberally." From a supplemental step; needs subject-matter confirmation.

checks.text: The lubricant used is a vegetable soap liquid, not a petroleum product, for hose rated for Skydrol/HYJET service.
checks.src: Caution: "Do not use any petroleum product with hose designed for synthetic fluids... use a vegetable soap liquid." Requires hose lay line and lubricant SDS; supplemental step, confirm with SME.

checks.text: Lubricant is applied to full depth of the socketed hose end and around the entire thread circumference, not a single spot dab.
checks.src: "Lubricate inside of hose and nipple threads liberally" — coverage only evidenced while applying. Supplemental step; needs SME confirmation.

checks.text: The hose bore and threads are free of grit, chips or rag lint carried in with the lubricant.
checks.src: Procedure sheet FOD box and rag provisions imply contamination control; no handbook figure for this step. Provisional supplemental step.

errors.text: Petroleum-based oil or grease used as assembly lubricant on a Skydrol/HYJET-rated hose, which looks correctly lubricated but degrades the inner tube.
Sparse or dry lubrication, so the nipple shears, rolls or extrudes the inner tube during insertion.
Excess lubricant runs onto the wire braid or picks up FOD that is driven into the hose bore.

steps.text: Screw the nipple into the socket with a wrench on the nipple hex, leaving .005" to .031" clearance between the nipple hex and the socket.

checks.text: Clearance between the nipple hex and the socket face measures between .005" and .031".
checks.src: Fig. 9-35 step 5: "leave .005" to .031" clearance between nipple hex and socket"; feeler gauge or shim stock required.

checks.text: A continuous gap remains all the way around the joint; the hex is not bottomed metal-to-metal on the socket.
checks.src: Derived from the required ".005" to .031" clearance"; only presence of a gap, not its size, is visible. Supplemental step needs SME confirmation.

checks.text: Nipple hex flats and socket are unmarred — no rounding, gouging or slipped-wrench scoring.
checks.src: Handbook directs "using wrench on hex of nipple"; reusable MS fittings per p.9-21 "may be detached and reused if they are not damaged". Inference from supplemental step.

checks.text: If the assembly is fabricated per MIL-H-8790, the exposed wire braid is coated with the specified sealant.
checks.src: "Hose assemblies fabricated per MIL-H-8790 must have the exposed wire braid coated with a special sealant"; hose spec read from lay line/paperwork.

errors.text: Nipple run fully home, bottoming the hex on the socket and crushing the inner tube — looks like a tight, correct joint.
Nipple left short so clearance exceeds .031", leaving the hose under-gripped and liable to blow off under pressure.
Wrench applied to the socket or B-nut instead of the nipple hex, rounding or scoring the fitting so it cannot be reused.

steps.text: Cap or plug the assembly and connect it to the test stand, bleeding all trapped air before tightening when testing with a liquid.

checks.text: Both ends of the hose assembly are closed — one capped or plugged, the other connected to the test stand port.
checks.src: Supplemental step 1; handbook mentions only 'tightening the cap or plug' without stating connection arrangement. Provisional, needs SME confirmation.

checks.text: All trapped air was bled from the assembly before the cap or plug was tightened for a liquid test.
checks.src: Handbook p.9-19: "When testing with a liquid, all trapped air is bled from the assembly prior to tightening the cap or plug."

checks.text: The test medium matches the hose's service per the manufacturer's instructions for that assembly.
checks.src: "hydraulic, fuel, and oil lines are generally tested using hydraulic oil or water, whereas air or instrument lines are tested with dry, oil-free air or nitrogen"; "follow the hose manufacturer's instructions".

checks.text: If a gas medium is used, the assembly is fully submerged in water before pressurization.
checks.src: "Hose tests, using a gas, are conducted underwater." Handbook extract reached via supplemental step, so provisional pending SME review.

errors.text: Cap or plug tightened with air still trapped in a liquid-filled assembly, giving a compressible, invalid and hazardous proof test.
Wrong test medium selected — e.g. petroleum hydraulic oil in a Skydrol hose, or unfiltered shop air in an instrument line.
Cap, plug or stand fitting loose or wrong dash size, so the assembly leaks at the closure instead of holding pressure.

steps.text: Apply the proof-test pressure specified by the hose manufacturer for the assembly.

checks.text: The pressure applied equals the proof-test pressure the hose manufacturer specifies for this assembly.
checks.src: Handbook: "in all cases, follow the hose manufacturer's instructions for proof-test pressure and fluid to be used"; step itself is supplemental, unreviewed.

checks.text: A repaired or overhauled assembly using existing hardware is pressurized to at least 1.5 times system pressure.
checks.src: Handbook: "it is recommended that the hose be tested to at least 1.5 system pressure" before installation on the aircraft.

checks.text: The gauge reading reached does not exceed the maximum proof pressure listed for that hose part number.
checks.src: Figure 9-37 lists "Max. Proof Pressure (PSI)" per MIL part number; supplemental step wording is unreviewed.

checks.text: Full test pressure is reached and held steady, not momentarily spiked, while the assembly is observed.
checks.src: Handbook: "All flexible hose must be proof-tested after assembly and applying pressure to the inside of the hose assembly."

errors.text: An arbitrary round pressure is used instead of the manufacturer's specified proof pressure; assembly looks tested but is unverified.
Pressure is driven above the maximum proof pressure, weakening the hose with no visible external damage.
Test is stopped short of full proof pressure or the gauge is misread, so the assembly is recorded as passed.

steps.text: Inspect the assembly under pressure and confirm it holds proof pressure without leaking.

checks.text: The gauge shows the manufacturer's specified proof pressure reached and held without decay during the test.
checks.src: "All flexible hose must be proof-tested after assembly"; "follow the hose manufacturer's instructions for proof-test pressure". Provisional; needs SME confirmation.

checks.text: A repaired or overhauled assembly using existing hardware and new hose is tested to at least 1.5 times system pressure.
checks.src: "it is recommended that the hose be tested to at least 1.5 system pressure"; system pressure value comes from paperwork. Provisional, needs SME confirmation.

checks.text: No leakage, weeping or bubbling appears at the nipple/socket junction, cap or braid while the assembly is held at pressure.
checks.src: Handbook requires proof test "by applying pressure to the inside of the hose assembly"; gas tests "are conducted underwater". Provisional, needs SME confirmation.

checks.text: After depressurizing, the fitting ends and braid are dry with no fluid staining or wet seepage tracks.
checks.src: Residue is the visible trace of the leakage the handbook's proof test is meant to detect. Provisional, needs SME confirmation.

errors.text: Assembly is pressurized to system pressure only, or an arbitrary pressure, and logged as proof-tested.
Pressure is applied with trapped air still in the assembly, masking a slow leak and creating a stored-energy hazard.
Seepage at the nipple hex is wiped off and the assembly is passed as dry.
Gas test performed in open air rather than underwater, so small leaks go undetected.
